record.original_question: How can time-fractional differential equations involving general fractional derivatives of arbitrary order be developed and analyzed so that they model processes that are intermediate between diffusion and wave propagation?

evidence.quote: Consider the time-fractional differential equations with the GFDs of arbitrary order to model, for instance, the processes intermediate between diffusion and wave propagation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Let $k\in L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}_+)$ be a nonnegative locally integrable kernel. For a function $f:\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{R}$, define the general fractional integral (GFI) with kernel $k$ by
$$ (\mathbb{I}_{(k)} f)(t)=\int_0^t k(t-\tau)f(\tau)\,d\tau, \qquad t>0. $$
For a Sonine kernel pair $(k,\kappa)$ — that is, a pair satisfying the Sonine condition $\int_0^t k(t-\tau)\kappa(\tau)\,d\tau=1$ for $t>0$ — the general fractional derivative (GFD) in the Riemann–Liouville sense is
$$ (\mathbb{D}_{(\kappa)} f)(t)=\frac{d}{dt}\int_0^t \kappa(t-\tau)f(\tau)\,d\tau, $$
and in the Caputo sense
$$ ({}_*\mathbb{D}_{(\kappa)} f)(t)=\int_0^t \kappa(t-\tau)f'(\tau)\,d\tau. $$
Suppose furthermore that a notion of GFD "of arbitrary order" greater than one has been defined via a generalized Sonine condition that produces kernels with an integrable singularity at the origin and that permits the prescription of two or more initial conditions in associated Cauchy problems.

Problem. Develop a theory of time-fractional partial differential equations of the form
$$ ({}_*\mathbb{D}_{(\kappa)} u)(x,t) = \mathcal{L}\, u(x,t), \qquad x\in\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n,\ t>0, $$
where $\mathcal{L}$ is a (possibly second-order elliptic) spatial operator and $\kappa$ is the kernel of a general fractional derivative of arbitrary order strictly between $1$ and $2$, with two initial conditions
$$ u(x,0)=\varphi(x),\qquad u_t(x,0)=\psi(x). $$
Specifically: (i) formulate the well-posed initial(-boundary) value problem; (ii) establish existence, uniqueness, and regularity of solutions; (iii) derive a fundamental solution and analyze its qualitative behaviour (positivity, asymptotics, propagation speed); and (iv) prove that the resulting evolution genuinely interpolates between the diffusive regime (single first-order initial condition) and the wave regime (two initial conditions with finite propagation speed) — that is, identify quantitative criteria on $\kappa$ under which the solutions exhibit behaviour intermediate between heat-like diffusion and undamped wave propagation.
artifact.status_search_result: A follow-up program has appeared: general fractional integrals and derivatives of arbitrary order have been defined via a generalized Sonine condition, with two fundamental theorems of fractional calculus and Cauchy problems admitting multiple initial conditions formulated. Subsequent works (e.g., on GFDs of arbitrary order in the Riemann–Liouville sense, 2022, and on multi-kernel extensions of Luchko's operational calculus, 2025) have advanced the theory. However, a complete theory of time-fractional PDEs with GFDs of arbitrary order modeling intermediate diffusion-wave processes (fundamental solutions, well-posedness, qualitative interpolation properties) remains in development and only partially settled.

status_evidence.title: General Fractional Integrals and Derivatives of Arbitrary Order
status_evidence.snippet: Extension of GFIs and GFDs to arbitrary order via a generalized Sonine condition; kernels have integrable singularities at zero; initial-value problems with several initial conditions can be formulated.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational framework for GFDs of arbitrary order, enabling multiple initial conditions needed for intermediate diffusion-wave models.

status_evidence.title: Fractional Differential Equations with the General Fractional Derivatives of Arbitrary Order in the Riemann-Liouville Sense
status_evidence.snippet: Follow-up developing fractional ODEs with GFDs of arbitrary order in the RL sense.
status_evidence.claim: Theory partially developed for ODE-level equations; PDE applications to intermediate processes still being investigated.

status_evidence.title: Extension of Luchko operational calculus to multi-Kernel general fractional derivatives
status_evidence.snippet: 2025 extension of Luchko operational calculus to multi-kernel GFDs.
status_evidence.claim: Recent advances continue to extend the analytical toolkit for GFDs of arbitrary order.
